title: The State of Independent Home-Service Trades Websites 2026
note: Aggregates computed from automated scans. No individual site is identified.
attribution: Free to use and cite under CC BY 4.0. Credit Clikiti with a link.
citation: Clikiti. (2026, October 15). The state of independent home-service trades websites 2026 (Q4 2026) [Report]. https://clikiti.com/research/trades/2026-q4
audience: Web agencies and freelancers selling to independent plumbing, HVAC, electrical, roofing and appliance repair businesses
findings: Only 17% of the 165 independent home-service trade websites we scanned state a warranty with its terms: on parts or labour, in months or years.
A typical site answers four of the nine questions homeowners ask before choosing (mean 4).
The median overall score is 77 out of 100 (mean 78).
The least-answered questions are "What if it fails again?" (17%), "What will the visit cost?" (18%) and "Can I spread the cost?" (27%).
The best-answered are "Do you work in my area?" (80%) and "How do I reach you, and when are you open?" (64%).
By kind of business, the highest median score is 83 (appliance repair and handyman), against 75 for plumbing and hvac, 75 for electrical and 75 for roofing and exteriors.
93% fail "Loads in under 2.5 s on a phone" (Core Web Vitals · LCP).
61% fail "Plumber, HVACBusiness, Electrician or RoofingContractor structured data" (Schema.org · HomeAndConstructionBusiness).

technical.label: Loads in under 2.5 s on a phone
Plumber, HVACBusiness, Electrician or RoofingContractor structured data

agencyProblems.label: Loads in under 2.5 s on a phone
agencyProblems.fix: Resize and compress the hero image, defer scripts, aim for under 2.5 s on a phone.
agencyProblems.pitch: Your home page takes several seconds to appear on the phone of someone standing in a flooded basement.

agencyProblems.label: Warranty or guarantee stated with its terms
agencyProblems.question: What if it fails again?
agencyProblems.fix: State the warranty on parts and on labour, in months or years, on the home page and the service pages.
agencyProblems.pitch: "What if it fails again?" is the second question a homeowner asks, and your site has no answer.

agencyProblems.label: A price shown: a service call, a fee, a rate or a job
agencyProblems.question: What will the visit cost?
agencyProblems.fix: Publish the service-call or diagnostic fee, and a starting price or range for the common jobs.
agencyProblems.pitch: Homeowners fear the bill first. Your site gives them no number at all, not even the trip charge.

agencyProblems.label: Financing offered
agencyProblems.question: Can I spread the cost?
agencyProblems.fix: A financing page that names the lender and the terms, linked from big-ticket service pages.
agencyProblems.pitch: A new furnace or roof is a five-figure decision. Your site never says it can be paid monthly.

agencyProblems.label: Text contrast passes 4.5:1
agencyProblems.fix: Raise text contrast to at least 4.5:1 in the theme.
agencyProblems.pitch: Parts of the site are hard to read, and it is a WCAG failure.
